moreDetails.architecture: Hill-embedded shrine with regional stone and mandapa elements.

name: Rameswara Swamy Temple
story: Ancient temple dedicated to Lord Shiva as Rameswara, believed to have been installed by Lord Rama.
highlight: The towering gopuram and intricate carvings.
entryNotes: Famous for its Lingam.

moreDetails.history: Dates back several centuries.
moreDetails.architecture: Dravidian style.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: A significant pilgrimage site in West Godavari.

name: Bala Brahmeswara Swamy Temple (The Western Gateway node, anchored in the Alampur Navabrahma complex)

moreDetails.architecture: Natural rock-cut cave shrines with carved panels.

name: Koteshwar Mahadev
story:
Koteshwar is a small village and the location of an ancient Shiva temple. It located near the mouth of Kori Creek, in the west of  Kutch district of Gujarat, India.
In past, the temple was almost entirely cut off from the mainland by tidal creeks but now is connected by road. Koteshwar Mahady is said to be the Bhairava of Hinglaj Mata residing at Hinglaj.

name: Wadapally Agastheshwara Temple

highlight: The sheer density of temples in one village.
entryNotes: 10km from Midnapore town.

moreDetails.history: Built between 1732 and late 18th century.
moreDetails.architecture: Chala and Ratna styles.
moreDetails.darshan: Heritage walk.
moreDetails.seasonal: Avoid summer heat.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Visit the Navaratna Shiva temple.
moreDetails.festivals: Shivratri.

name: Rampara Kalibari
story: A village Kali temple in Rampara dedicated to Siddheshwari Kali and celebrated for its Kali Puja.
highlight: Traditional Bengal temple courtyard and festival worship.
timings: Open daily; timings vary by season.
entryNotes: Located in Rampara, Hooghly district.

moreDetails.history: Rampara Kalibari is a Kali temple in Hooghly district built by the Nandy family and dedicated to Siddheshwari Kali.

name: Nandikeshwari Temple
story: A major Shakti Peetha where the necklace of Sati fell. The main deity is worshipped as a rock smeared with vermilion.
highlight: One of the 51 Shakti Peethas.
entryNotes: In Sainthia town.

moreDetails.history: Ancient pilgrimage site.
moreDetails.architecture: Simple Bengal style.
moreDetails.darshan: Spiritual.
moreDetails.seasonal: Crowded during Puja.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Visit the Shiva temple in the complex too.
moreDetails.festivals: Navratri.

name: Jaleswar Shiva Temple
story: The tallest temple in Santipur, built by the Nadia Raj family. It features exquisite terracotta and a massive structure.
highlight: The towering height and the history of the Nadia royals.
entryNotes: In Santipur town.

moreDetails.history: Built by Raja Raghuram Ray in the 18th century.
moreDetails.architecture: Char-chala/At-chala hybrid.
moreDetails.darshan: Devotional.
moreDetails.seasonal: Crowded during Rash.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Santipur is famous for sarees too.
moreDetails.festivals: Rash Yatra.

name: Sevoke Shiva Mandir
story: Located near the iconic Coronation Bridge, this temple (often called Sevoke Kalibari but houses Shiva) offers stunning views of the Teesta River.
highlight: Panoramic view of Teesta river and the mountains.
entryNotes: Many stairs to climb.

moreDetails.history: Built in the mid-20th century.
moreDetails.architecture: Hill style.
moreDetails.darshan: Scenic.
moreDetails.seasonal: Monsoon view is dramatic.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Beware of monkeys.
moreDetails.festivals: Navratri.

story: A historic Kali temple by the Hooghly river at Shyamnagar, associated with the Mulajore Kalibari traditions.
highlight: Riverside shrine with long local heritage.
timings: Open daily; timings vary by season.
entryNotes: Set near the Hooghly riverbanks in Shyamnagar.

highlight: Detailed terracotta panels on all three temples.
entryNotes: Near Katwa.

moreDetails.history: Built by the Chandra family in the 19th century.
moreDetails.architecture: Pancha-ratna and Rekha styles.
moreDetails.darshan: Artistic.
moreDetails.seasonal: Pleasant in winter.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Ask locals for the key if closed.
moreDetails.festivals: Shivratri.

name: Shantinath Shiva Temple
story: Built by the famous Mitra Mustafi family, this temple is a showcase of fine terracotta craftsmanship.
highlight: The terracotta panels showing social scenes.
entryNotes: Near Balagarh.

moreDetails.history: Built in the 18th century.
moreDetails.architecture: At-chala.
moreDetails.darshan: Artistic.
moreDetails.seasonal: Pleasant.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: The Chandimandap nearby is also famous.

name: Supur Jora Shiva Mandir
story: Twin Shiva temples (Jora Mandir) built in the 18th century. One is octagonal (ridgeless Rekha) and the other is circular, both with stunning terracotta.
highlight: The rare octagonal and circular designs.
entryNotes: Near Bolpur.

moreDetails.history: Built by local zamindars in the 18th-19th century.
moreDetails.architecture: Mixed styles (Rekha/Chala).
moreDetails.darshan: Historic.
moreDetails.seasonal: Crowded during Poush Mela.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Often called the 'Twin Temples of Supur'.
moreDetails.festivals: Shivratri.

name: Surul Jora Shiva Temple
story: Located near Santiniketan, these twin temples feature some of the finest terracotta panels depicting Ramayana scenes.
highlight: Detailed terracotta work right near the tourist hub of Santiniketan.
entryNotes: 3km from Bolpur.

moreDetails.history: Built in the 19th century by the Sarkar family.
moreDetails.architecture: Pancha-ratna.
moreDetails.darshan: Artistic.
moreDetails.seasonal: Crowded during Poush Mela.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Visit the Sarkar Rajbari next door.

entryNotes: Located near the Roopnarayana river in Tamluk.

name: Taraknath Temple (Tarakeswar)
story: A major Shaiva pilgrimage shrine in Tarakeswar revered as Baba Taraknath.
highlight: Pilgrim gatherings in Shravan and a lively temple precinct.

entryNotes: Expect larger crowds during Shravan.

moreDetails.puranicView: Shiva is worshipped here as Taraknath, with strong pilgrimage traditions.

name: Tarapith Temple
story: A famed Shakta shrine in Tarapith dedicated to Maa Tara and revered as a Shakti Peetha.
highlight: A vibrant temple town anchored by Tara worship.
bestTime: Kali Puja and Tara Puja seasons; early mornings are calmer.
timings: Open daily; timings vary by season.
entryNotes: Expect long queues during festival days.

moreDetails.history: Tarapith Temple is a major Shakta shrine in Birbhum dedicated to Goddess Tara and recognized as a Shakti Peetha and Siddha Peetha.
moreDetails.architecture: Bengal chala-style temple architecture within a dense pilgrimage town.
moreDetails.darshan: Darshan is open throughout the day; aarti draws the biggest crowds.
moreDetails.seasonal: Festival seasons are the busiest for pilgrims.
moreDetails.visitorNotes: Plan extra time during Kali Puja and Tara Puja.
moreDetails.festivals: Tara Puja · Kali Puja · Durga Puja

highlight: Riverside navaratna architecture near Rasmani Ghat.
timings: Open daily; timings vary by season.
entryNotes: Located near Rasmani Ghat on the Hooghly riverbank.
